newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Baptist minister takes sex to the ballpark.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Baptist minister takes sex to the ballpark.

text.p: A Baptist minister in Texas is calling on young men to clean up their sex act and hopes to win them over by taking them to a baseball game.

Richard Ellis, a minister at the First Baptist Church in Dallas, plans to run a straight-talking seminar on sexual issues at the Texas Rangers' ballpark on Sept. 28. Any man paying the $25 to get into the seminar will get a ticket to watch the evening game.
"It's going to be locker room talk from a Christian perspective," Ellis, 36, said in an interview on Wednesday. "The ballpark is a place where guys feel at ease."

He said the three-hour seminar, called "Hits, Runs and Errors", would take place at the ballpark's museum auditorium and that the participants would then go straight on to "get a hot dog and watch the game."
Ellis said many men struggled with sex issues and that his ballpark seminar was a way of making the biblical view on sexual relations more accessible to young men.

"I know there are a lot of people who think Christians don't even know what sex is but I want single men to know God has a lot to say on the subject," he said in a statement advertising the event. "God has a perfect plan for sex -- not the cheap, slick Madison Avenue version of sex but the God-ordained union of one man and one woman."
Ellis said casual sexual relationships might bring a quick thrill but often wreck homes, bring unwanted pregnancies, spread diseases like AIDS and can lead men and women into despair.
"Just because society tells a young man to score as many sexual home runs as he can doesn't mean he'll win the game that way," he said.
The ballpark's museum auditorium holds a maximum 300 people but Ellis said the intitial response had been impressive and he might move the seminar to a nearby conference room or hotel ballroom.
While catching the ballgame would be a key part of the day, Ellis said he would not be encouraging seminar-goers to wash down their hot dogs with a beer. "It'll probably be a dry event," he said.
